title: When LeWM Misses the Color: Cue Binding in Tunnel Rooms
topic: 1. What makes a pretrained representation actionable?
4. How do we evaluate actionable representations?
5. What can go wrong when pretrained agents act?
TLDR: Tunnel Rooms reveals a gap between accurate tunnel localization and weak cue binding in LeWM, measured through probes, reconstructions, goal-energy landscapes, and planning.
abstract: A world model can learn where an object is without learning the detail that makes it useful for action. We introduce Tunnel Rooms Color, a navigation benchmark in which matching tunnel colors determine teleportation destinations. Reaching an image-specified goal by the direct route requires using color to choose the correct tunnel. We find that an adapted LeWorldModel (LeWM) learns tunnel locations accurately but represents their cue-dependent destinations much less reliably. Across variants, linear probes achieve mean $R^2$ above .90 for locations but only .20–.26 for cue-indexed coordinates; image reconstructions blur cue distinctions; and goal-energy maps assign low cost near both candidate tunnels in an illustrated scene. Planning is also difficult: success on the farther correct tunnel is 16–52% across Color, Shape, and a green/blue palette. Together, these observations make Tunnel Rooms a controlled case study of the gap between learning visual geometry and preserving the distinctions needed to act.
